status: prospective geometry-aware audit experiment locked before execution; synthetic controller validation, not learned-LLM evidence
research_question: Can a small trusted-label audit distinguish harmful from benign verifier optimization when policy-shift coordinates alone are identical or uninformative?
true_reward: Bernoulli(0.5), deterministic resampling until both classes occur

verifier_geometry.construction: same standardized trusted direction as equal_kl_alignment_stress; rho rotates fixed-norm verifier error

estimator: sample i~p with replacement; proxy score v(i) is free and its exact baseline mean is known; estimate Cov_p(y,v) by mean y_i*(v_i-E_p[v])
confidence_interval: two-sided Hoeffding using the exact support range of x=y*(v-E_p[v]); halfwidth=(x_max-x_min)*sqrt(log(2/delta)/(2n))
theorem_scope: for exponential proxy optimization, local trusted-progress derivative equals Cov_p(y,v); when the interval contains the true covariance, block/allow cannot have the wrong sign
primary_prediction: harmful block rate >=0.8, benign allow rate >=0.8, and wrong-sign decisive rate <=0.08 in each arm at n=128
reporting: all tasks and budgets retained; report exact covariance, CI, decision, block/allow/inconclusive rates and wrong-sign rates; no threshold selection after outcomes
comparison: a gate using only baseline policy KL sees KL=0 for both arms and cannot distinguish them; the audit is explicitly geometry-aware
scope: finite-support proof-of-concept for an audit controller; it uses trusted labels and exact proxy scores and does not claim an LLM verifier is calibrated this way
